answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may submit work, then slash that deposit if randomly sampled peers verify a false claim. One person can still mint many identities, but every extra account ties up more capital, and a detected lie destroys the stake rather than merely retiring an account. A falcon-like auditor can treat a plume of linked submissions as a signal to sample them more heavily, while keeping the penalty tied to evidence, not appearance alone.
